title: sessions: move unified workspace picker setting
body:
## Summary

- move the unified workspace picker setting from shared Chat into the Sessions chat contribution
- rename the setting from `chat.agentSessions.consolidatedRemoteWorkspaces` to `sessions.chat.unifiedWorkspacePicker.enabled`
- describe the complete experience controlled by the setting: consolidated GitHub and remote workspace sources, workspace search, and, when supported, the **No workspace** option
- update the workspace picker, new-session composer, and **New Quick Chat** action to consume the Sessions-owned setting

## Setting migration

The deprecated setting remains registered so application-scoped values can be loaded and migrated.

For each explicitly configured legacy value, the migration:

1. removes `chat.agentSessions.consolidatedRemoteWorkspaces`
2. copies its value to `sessions.chat.unifiedWorkspacePicker.enabled`
3. preserves an existing explicit value on the new setting rather than overwriting it

Defaults and remote experiment assignments are not persisted as user settings, so they are not copied by this migration.

## Experiment update

The setting uses the default treatment name derived from its new ID:

`config.sessions.chat.unifiedWorkspacePicker.enabled`

Because the existing experiment only recently started and has little data, restart it using this new treatment name rather than retaining the legacy identifier indefinitely:

1. stop the progression that publishes `config.chat.agentSessions.consolidatedRemoteWorkspaces`
2. create or update the replacement progression to publish `config.sessions.chat.unifiedWorkspacePicker.enabled`
3. use `false` for control and `true` for treatment
4. target builds containing this setting rename and the unified picker UX

Do not delete or rename a shared ExP variant that is used by other experiments; create the replacement flag/progression as required by ExP.

## Validation

title: Do not mark a denied subagent tool call as a subagent
body:
A denied `Agent` or `Task` call still gets a subagent marker attached to its result, so on restore the host registers a subagent chat whose transcript can never exist.

## What happens

`toolKind` is derived from the tool **name**, with no regard for the outcome, and `_attachToolResult` pushes `ToolResultContentType.Subagent` unconditionally. On restore, `_registerRestoredSubagentSummaries` scans replayed turns for that marker and registers a chat with a lazy resolver, and the resolver throws `Subagent transcript is not available yet` forever, because nothing was ever spawned.

Since #334312 that is no longer fatal to the session, but the phantom chat is still registered, still fails to `subscribe`, and still shows in the session's chat list as a subagent that never produces anything.

## How it was hit

Auto mode could not classify an `Agent` call and denied it:

```
"...temporarily unavailable, so auto mode cannot determine the safety of Agent right now..."
"toolDenialKind": "automode-unavailable"
```

The SDK transcript for that session is 47 lines with zero `isSidechain` entries, confirming no subagent ran. Any denial reaches this the same way, so a permission rule or a user rejecting the call does too.

## The change

`is_error` alone is not the right test: it also covers a subagent that **started and then failed**, and those children have real transcripts that must still be linked on restore.

The SDK stamps `agentId: <hex>` on the tool_result of a call that actually spawned, which is what `scanTranscriptForAgentIds` already keys on through the exported `SUBAGENT_ID_SUFFIX_REGEX`. A pre-spawn denial is therefore the case with an error and no agentId:

```ts
const spawned = !isError || SUBAGENT_ID_SUFFIX_REGEX.test(resultText);
if (isSubagent && spawned) {
```

`resultText` is already computed immediately above for the past-tense message, so nothing new is derived.

## Tests

- `Fixture 5c: a denied Agent tool_use produces no subagent marker` asserts the call is still recognised as a subagent by name, that `success` is `false`, and that no marker is attached.
- `Fixture 5d: an Agent that spawned and then failed keeps its subagent marker` is the failed-after-spawn case, and fails against an `is_error`-only condition.

Fixtures 5 and 5b continue to pass, so successful spawns are unchanged. The suite is 30 passing. No new type errors.

title: Fix terminal prompt duplication when resizing the terminal panel
body:
Fixes #329946 (partial — see "Known limitations" below)

## Summary

When the terminal panel is resized, the shell prompt can be duplicated / new prompt lines created on every resize instead of the buffer reflowing cleanly. Two causes in the terminal resize path:

1. **Redundant PTY resizes on every layout event.** `TerminalResizeDebouncer.resize()` fired a resize even when the grid dimensions did not change (e.g. while dragging the panel), sending a PTY resize (SIGWINCH) on every layout event. Shells repaint the prompt on SIGWINCH, so this produced a storm of prompt redraws while dragging.

2. **Horizontal resizes debounced too briefly.** The debounced horizontal resize fired after 100ms, but shells such as zsh need longer than that to fully process a prompt redraw after a resize. When resizes arrived back-to-back, the shell computed its prompt redraw from a stale terminal width, which misplaces the erase/rewrite and leaves duplicated prompt fragments in the buffer.

## Changes

`src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalResizeDebouncer.ts`:
- Skip the resize entirely (and cancel any pending debounced resize) when the requested `cols`/`rows` equal the current grid — no more redundant PTY resizes / SIGWINCH storms while dragging.
- Only fire the immediate Y-resize when `rows` actually changed, and only schedule the debounced X-resize when `cols` actually changed.
- Increase `DebounceResizeXDelay` from 100ms to 300ms so the shell's prompt redraw is fully processed between consecutive resizes.

## Verification

- Reproduced the duplication headlessly with a real zsh 5.9 and bash shell in a pty driving the bundled xterm.js: with the 100ms debounce the buffer ended with 3 prompt copies after a shrink/grow/shrink cycle; with 300ms exactly 1 copy.
- Verified in a running Code OSS instance (launched with playwright over CDP): resizing the bottom-panel terminal (long prompt, shrink/grow cycles, continuous drags) reflows cleanly with no duplication.

## Known limitations (honest assessment)

This fixes the common cases (panel resizing at moderate widths, continuous drags). It does **not** fix every duplication scenario:

- **Extreme-narrow terminals with colored prompts** (e.g. terminal docked in the side panel and shrunk to its minimum width, ~15-20 columns, with a colored `PS1`/`PROMPT`): the prompt can still duplicate. Root cause: xterm.js deliberately does not reflow the cursor line on non-Windows (`reflowCursorLine=false`), so the prompt is a single buffer row rendered wrapped across several visual rows. The shell's redraw (readline/zsh) operates on visual rows, so its erase/rewrite misses rows and fragments accumulate. Enabling `reflowCursorLine` makes this worse due to https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/5295 (cursor mispositioned on reflow of cursor line), which the xterm.js maintainers have declined to fix. Upstream VS Code has no fix for this either; it would require a change in xterm.js or readline.

- **Editor area** (empty canvas or empty tabs row) — middle-click opens a new terminal in the editor area, matching the existing double-click → new file. Middle-click on an empty editor group now opens a terminal instead of closing the group.

title: dictation: fix indefinite hangs by adding timeouts to Foundry Local native calls
body:
## What

On-device (`nemo`/Foundry Local) dictation could hang indefinitely with no error surfaced to the user — the toolbar spinner would just spin forever, or clicking Stop/Cancel would do nothing.

## Why

`LocalTranscriptionService` (the utility-process side of dictation) awaits several native `foundry-local-sdk` calls that have no `AbortSignal` and no timeout of their own:

- the model catalog lookup (`manager.catalog.getModel`)
- `model.load()` (explicitly called out in an existing code comment as having "no AbortSignal")
- `session.start()`
- each `session.append()` call — these are chained serially through `_appendChain` to preserve audio order, so one wedged append blocks every later chunk **and** `stop()`, which awaits the whole chain
- the result stream's `next()` (via `for await...of session.getStream()`) — `stop()` awaits the consumer promise, so a stream that silently stops yielding (without throwing) hangs Stop forever
- `session.stop()` / `session.dispose()`

If any of these stalls — a proxy/firewall silently dropping packets, a wedged native addon, a driver hiccup during model load, etc. — the corresponding promise never settles. Since `start()`/`pushAudio()`/`stop()`/`cancel()` all await these calls directly or transitively, the whole feature hangs with no recovery short of restarting VS Code.

The one existing exception was the native runtime tarball download, which already has a `DOWNLOAD_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS` guard (see `foundryLocalRuntime.ts`) — this PR extends the same pattern to the remaining unguarded native calls.

## Change

Adds a small `withTimeout()` helper and races each of the calls above against a bounded timeout (30s for catalog lookup, 120s for model load, 15s for session start/append/teardown, 60s inactivity for the result stream). A timeout now rejects with a descriptive error that flows through the existing error-handling path (`classifyModelError`, which gains a new `'timeout'` code) exactly like any other model/session failure, so the existing UI (progress ring, error notification, `_failModelSession`) picks it up instead of hanging silently.

This does not cancel the underlying native call (the SDK gives us no way to) — it only unblocks whichever caller is waiting on it so the failure is surfaced and the session can be reset/retried.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` passes (the one remaining reported error, in `mcpSamplingLog.test.ts`, is pre-existing and unrelated to this change).
- This service wraps a native addon with no existing unit test harness (only `foundryLocalRuntime` and `foundryLocalModelImport` have tests), so validation here is via typecheck + code review; the change is a set of surgical `Promise.race` wraps around existing await points and does not alter behavior on the non-timeout success path.

title: Clear stale focus and selection in the chat changed-files list
Fix tab close button stuck showing "Close Others" after focus changes
body:
## Description

Alt+hover swaps a tab's **Close** action for **Close Others**. Both inputs to that swap could go stale across a focus change: `redrawTabAction()` read `modifierKeyEmitter.keyStatus.altKey` at paint time (the Alt `keyup` is delivered to whichever app you Alt+Tab'd into), and `hoveredTabIndex` was only cleared by a real `mouseleave`. Coming back to the window without moving the mouse could therefore leave the `x` armed as "Close Others", so a plain click silently closed every other editor in the group.

### Changes — `MultiEditorTabsControl`

- **Local Alt state.** A `isAltPressed` field, fed by the `ModifierKeyEmitter` event, replaces the two on-demand reads of `modifierKeyEmitter.keyStatus.altKey`. It is the single source of truth for the swap and redraws the hovered tab when it flips.
- **Give up the swap on focus loss.** `IHostService.onDidChangeFocus(false)` clears both the Alt state and the hovered tab, so a hover left over from before the focus change cannot be re-armed by Alt state re-established on return. Re-hovering a tab arms it again as usual.
- **Re-validate Alt from mouse events.** `mousemove`/`mousedown` on the tabs container carry the real modifier state even when a `keyup` was missed entirely — this covers macOS Mission Control, where the window may never see a `blur`.

The mouse listeners are registered in the **capture** phase because `BaseActionViewItem` calls `EventHelper.stop(e, true)` on `mousedown`; a bubble-phase listener never sees a press on the close button itself, which is precisely the reported "click without moving the mouse" case.

```ts
for (const eventType of [EventType.MOUSE_MOVE, EventType.MOUSE_DOWN]) {
	this._register(addDisposableListener(tabsContainer, eventType, (e: MouseEvent) => {
		this.setAltPressed(e.altKey);
	}, true));
}
```

In the stale-Alt case the capture handler swaps the action item mid-`mousedown`, so that first click is swallowed rather than executing "Close Others" — the icon is then correct and the next click closes the single tab.

`EditorTabsControl.hostService` becomes `protected` so the subclass can use it.

### Tests

`src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts` covers the baseline swap plus the focus-loss, mouse-move and action-mousedown paths; each regression test was checked to fail with its corresponding part of the change reverted.

### Notes for reviewers

- After returning from another application the swap requires a fresh hover (move to another tab, or leave and re-enter). This is the behaviour suggested in the issue and is what makes a stale hover unexploitable.
- `menuEntryActionViewItem.ts` has the same latent staleness pattern; left untouched to keep this scoped to tabs.

title: feat: implementing word wrap indicators
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/47855 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a7be874-cb00-41a9-8d38-616456c31323 Adds an opt-in indicator at the wrapping column of every soft wrapped line, so a wrap can be told apart from a real line break. Addresses #47855. Off by default. Set `editor.wordWrapIndicator` to `true` to turn it on; it only has an effect while `editor.wordWrap` is enabled. ## How it works ### Rendering Rendering is done by `WordWrapIndicatorOverlay`, a `DynamicViewOverlay` registered on the content overlay layer in `view.ts` alongside the selection and whitespace overlays. `prepareRender` walks the view lines of the viewport and produces one HTML string per line. A line gets a glyph only when `continuesWithWrappedLine` is set — that is, when it is followed by a soft wrap rather than by a real line break, and is not the last line of the model. The glyph itself is a single `
` holding U+21A9 LEFTWARDS ARROW WITH HOOK. Its content-relative `left` is the effective wrapping column multiplied by the font's typical half-width character width, so every glyph stays aligned with the boundary that produced the wrap. Horizontal scrolling moves the glyph with the document content instead of pinning it to the viewport edge. Its height comes from `getLineHeightForLineNumber`, so lines carrying a custom line height keep the indicator vertically aligned. ### Color `editorWordWrapIndicator.foreground` is a new theme colour that defaults to `editorWhitespace.foreground`, so out of the box the indicator is as muted as rendered whitespace, while themes can still override it on its own. ## Known Limitations The indicator marks the wrapping boundary rather than the exact end of the rendered text, so a segment that wraps at whitespace can leave a gap before the glyph. When a fixed `wordWrapColumn` lies beyond the viewport, the indicator remains offscreen until horizontal scrolling reveals that column. The indicator is a visual-only overlay; it has no equivalent representation for screen readers or the minimap. ## Other Editors - Visual Studio - Notepad++ - IntelliJ IDEA Word wrap indicator is shown at the beginning of the wrapped line Does not have word wrap indicator: - XCode - Sublime Text --- ## Manual checklist before marking ready for review - [x] Toggle `editor.wordWrapIndicator` live with a wrapped file open: the glyph appears and disappears without needing a reload. - [x] Glyph stays aligned with the effective wrapping column at several `editor.fontSize` values and with a proportional font (`editor.fontFamily` set to a non-monospace family). - [x] Correct with variable line heights. - [x] Interacts sanely with `editor.renderWhitespace: 'all'` — the glyph should not collide with a trailing whitespace dot. - [x] Not selectable and not copied when selecting across a wrapped line (`pointer-events: none` covers hit testing; verify the clipboard). - [x] Inline suggestions / inlay hints / injected text on a wrapped line do not push the glyph to the wrong position. - [x] `editorWordWrapIndicator.foreground` shows up in `workbench.colorCustomizations` IntelliSense and overriding it takes effect. - [x] Legible in Dark+, Light+, and both high contrast themes — the inherited `editorWhitespace.foreground` is deliberately faint, so confirm it is visible enough in HC without being noisy in the default themes. - [x] Accessibility: confirm the glyph is not announced by the screen reader as line content. ## Feedback from standup Team members mentioned in the standup that they would prefer having the word wrap indicator on the left-hand side in the gutter instead of at the wrapping column on the right. The issue with this idea is that it requires the gutter to be present, so people with no gutter would not see this, and sometimes people only show every 5 lines so the word wrap indicator would look weird.

title: Copy the image when using Copy in a webview context menu
body: Fixes #292567 ### Problem Right clicking an image in a webview and choosing **Copy** puts nothing on the clipboard. Selecting the image first and then copying works, which is the clue to what is going on. The webview context menu's `Copy` is the standard `CopyAction`, routed to `webview.copy()` in `webview.contribution.ts`, which sends an `execCommand` message that the webview shell runs as `contentDocument.execCommand('copy')`. That only ever copies the *text selection*. Right clicking an image does not create a selection, so there is nothing to copy — and no error, which is why the issue reports silence rather than a failure. ### Fix Track the element the context menu was opened on in `pre/index.html`. When `copy` arrives with a collapsed selection and that element is an ``, encode it as a png and write it with `navigator.clipboard.write` instead of running `execCommand`. Details worth noting: - **Selection still wins.** If the user actually has something selected we fall straight through to `execCommand`, so selecting an image and copying behaves exactly as before. Cut, paste, undo and redo are untouched. - **Cross origin images.** Most webview images are served by the webview service worker, which synthesises the response, so drawing them into a canvas works directly. An image fetched from a genuinely opaque cross origin response taints the canvas and `toBlob` throws, so we fall back to re-requesting it in cors mode and going through `createImageBitmap`. - **Focus.** `navigator.clipboard.write` rejects unless the document is focused, and copy is dispatched as the context menu is closing. We give focus a moment to come back, but still attempt the write if it does not, so we never silently do nothing. - **Staleness.** The tracked image is cleared on the next click or keypress, so a later keyboard copy with nothing selected does not resurrect an image the user right clicked earlier. ### Testing The two encode paths were measured in a webview on VS Code 1.108 with a probe extension: drawing a `vscode-resource` image into a canvas succeeds (`ok: true`), and the cors re-fetch fallback also succeeds (`fetchStatus: 200`, `ok: true`). The end to end context menu flow has not been exercised against a build of this branch — I would appreciate a check on Windows and Linux in particular, where the context menu is rendered differently and the focus timing may not match macOS. ### Related The same missing cors fallback exists in three other copy-image implementations that each grew independently — `markdown-language-features`, `media-preview`, and the notebook webview. A remote image in a markdown preview fails there today with `SecurityError: Tainted canvases may not be exported`. Not touched here; happy to follow up if it is worth consolidating.

<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Run wherever Linux Docker is available**: The suite probes `docker info` for a reachable daemon with `OSType=linux`. title: agentHost: Keep passive session opens from changing recency
body:
## Summary

- suppress the SDK `session.resume` event when Agent Host cold-opens an existing Copilot session
- keep observational session opens from advancing the persisted session modification time
- cover the resume configuration passed by the Copilot session launcher

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/334501

## Problem

The Sessions view can show an old session as modified recently even though its last message was sent days ago.

For Copilot sessions, the displayed `updatedAt` ultimately comes from the SDK/runtime `modifiedTime`, which is based on the `events.jsonl` modification time. Cold-opening a session calls `resumeSession`; publishing a `session.resume` event can modify that journal, making a passive open look like recent user activity.

## Resolution

Agent Host now passes `suppressResumeEvent: true` when it resumes an existing session for display. This lets the runtime restore the live session without recording an observational resume event that changes recency.

## Dependency

**Blocked by https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/18323. Do not merge until VS Code consumes a runtime release containing that change.**

The current runtime couples resume-event suppression with resume-state processing. Runtime PR #18323 separates those concerns so suppressed resumes still restore model/context and preserve orphan and pending-work semantics while avoiding journal writes, subscriber publication, and modified-time updates.

## Validation

title: Agent Host: Use VS Code certificates for Dev Container CLI
body:
## Summary

Configure the bundled Dev Container CLI to use the certificates loaded by VS Code, including enterprise system certificates and user-provided `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`.

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Do not force Node `--use-system-ca`**: That runtime switch would bypass VS Code certificate settings. The CLI instead receives a `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` bundle, matching the approach used by the Remote Containers extension.
- **Reuse VS Code certificate policy**: Certificate loading goes through `IRequestService.loadCertificates()`, while `http.systemCertificates` gates whether system certificates are added. The request service also honors `http.systemCertificatesNode`.
- **Preserve explicit environment configuration**: A valid existing `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` value wins and is passed through unchanged.
- **Use a VS Code-owned temporary namespace**: Generated content-addressed PEM files are cached under `<tmpDir>/vscode-dev-container`, rather than the Remote Containers extension-specific `vsch` directory.
- **Handle concurrent writers safely**: Each process writes a unique temporary file and atomically renames it to the certificate-content hash. A rename failure is accepted only when another process has already published the expected target.

</details>

## Changes

- Inject the shared-process request service into the Dev Container Agent Host launcher.
- Resolve the Dev Container CLI environment once per process.
- Preserve valid `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` or generate a hashed PEM file from VS Code-loaded certificates.

title: Keep auto experiment defaults applied when assignments are refetched
body:
This stops experiment-driven setting defaults from being dropped and re-applied whenever assignments are refetched, which made the workbench visibly blink between the classic and Modern UI layouts shortly after startup.

### Changes

- `ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution` now keeps an experiment default that is already registered with the same resolved value, instead of re-evaluating it and deregistering it.
- This fixes an oscillation: the configuration registry mutates `property.default` to reflect registered default overrides, so once an `auto` experiment was applied, the next resolution compared the treatment against itself, concluded it matched the default, and removed the override. `WorkbenchAssignmentService` fires `onDidRefetchAssignments` shortly after the initial assignment fetch, so this happened during startup — `workbench.experimental.modernUI` flipped back to `false`, `updateFloatingPanels()` stripped the `modern-ui` classes, and a later refetch flipped it back.
- `shouldOverride` is deliberately left unchanged. Comparing against the schema-authored default instead would silently drop a control-arm assignment whenever another non-experiment `configurationDefaults` override exists for the same key, and would make `preventExperimentOverride` redundant.
- Startup-mode latching, the `preventExperimentOverride` guard, the Agents window `agentsWindow.default` comparison, and removal when a treatment resolves to `undefined` are all unaffected.
- Added regression coverage for an auto experiment surviving a refetch, and for a control-arm value still winning over an unrelated default override.

### Validation

title: Agent Host: provide inline editor context before send
body:
## Summary

- Actualize a bounded source window for editor inline chat inside the Agent Host immediately before provider dispatch.
- Keep the protocol selection attachment and browser/UI state unchanged.
- Mark `<editor_inline_context>` as current, authoritative source and tell the model to edit directly without a redundant read when it has sufficient context.
- Scope the behavior to the existing Agent Host chat-surface contribution.

The injected context is bounded to 16 lines, 220 characters per line, 4,096 rendered characters, and a 1 MiB source read. The target attachment is matched against the editor-inline surface URI so another selected attachment cannot be used accidentally.

## Performance investigation

We profiled repeated `comment out this line` requests in editor inline chat using Agent Host debug logs and CPU profiles.

| Stage | Original | Context only | Context + authoritative instruction | Final delta vs. original |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Session ready | 1.662s | 1.201s | 0.960s | -0.702s |
| Provider begins | 8.771s | 7.197s | 7.615s | -1.156s |
| First model call | 5.709s | 5.488s | 6.111s | +0.402s |
| `view` tool | 1.274s | 1.154s | eliminated | -1.274s |
| Tool-planning model call after `view` | 3.585s | 10.593s | eliminated | -3.585s |
| `edit` tool | 0.784s | 0.763s | 1.379s | +0.595s |
| Final model call | 3.056s | 2.936s | 2.707s | -0.349s |
| **Total** | **23.289s** | **28.241s** | **17.907s** | **-5.382s (-23.1%)** |

With context alone, the model still requested `view` for almost exactly the lines already present in `<editor_inline_context>`. After strengthening the instruction, the first model response was the `edit` call and the redundant `view` plus follow-up planning round trip disappeared.

The CPU captures were approximately 91-93% idle/program/GC, so the latency is dominated by SDK/runtime and model waits rather than Agent Host CPU work.

## MCP investigation and follow-up

The traces also showed roughly seven seconds before the first provider turn while 13 MCP servers started, authenticated, or failed/retried. This happened even though the session was definitively marked `vscode.chat.ephemeralSession: true`.

We tested all of the following for ephemeral sessions:

1. `enableConfigDiscovery: false`
2. omitting `mcpServers` instead of sending `{}`
3. additionally omitting `pluginDirectories`

None changed MCP startup: the same 13 servers still launched, including Azure, GitHub, Slack/WorkIQ, `vscode-tools`, `context7`, and the failing/retrying Docker-backed `awesome-copilot` server. The first request also remained around 45.8k uncached input tokens.

Those VS Code-side MCP experiments have been rolled back from this PR. We should instead add a Copilot SDK session option that acts as a master MCP switch: when disabled, the runtime must not discover, start, authenticate, or expose any MCP server regardless of config-directory discovery, plugin directories, explicit server maps, or runtime defaults. VS Code can then set that option for ephemeral inline-chat sessions.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Focused Agent Host suites previously passed 388 tests during implementation.
- After the final instruction update, 372 tests passed and one stale expected-instruction assertion failed; that assertion was updated before commit and was not rerun at the requester's direction.
- Pre-commit hygiene passed for all changed files.

title: agentHost: Resolve published MCP server lifecycle IDs
body:
Fixes #332072

## Problem

Agent Host start/stop handling reverse-resolved customization IDs only through the controller's runtime `_live` inventory. During a same-name collision, the runtime can first associate a server name with a published plugin child and then receive a distinct same-name workspace top-level customization.

Agent Customizations presents the workspace entry and sends its exact ID, but the live lookup no longer recognizes that ID. The provider logs `Cannot start unknown MCP server customization ...`, no server process starts, and the optimistic client reducer leaves the row at `Starting`.

## Change

Keep the runtime lookup as the first choice, then fall back to an exact-ID lookup across the session's currently published customizations.

The fallback accepts only an ID that is present in current session state. It does not add a broad same-name alias and does not change collision precedence. The SDK lifecycle API remains name-keyed, so it starts the effective server winner already selected for that name.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client`
- `npx mocha test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --timeout=20000 --exit --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/shared/mcpCustomizationController.test.ts` — 20 passing
- Targeted ESLint and `git diff --check`
- Regression coverage verifies published IDs resolve before the SDK has populated the live inventory and unknown IDs remain rejected.
- Deterministic live Code OSS A/B with a real Copilot Agent Host session and real local stdio MCP processes:
  - A host-only plugin published and started `dupe`; the real UI then stopped it through its plugin-child customization ID.
  - A workspace-root `.mcp.json` with another `dupe` was published afterward, producing two distinct current customization IDs with no synthetic `mcp-top-level:*` ID and no intervening SDK state event that could repair the mapping.
  - Unpatched main: the UI dispatched `SessionMcpServerStartRequested` with the exact workspace ID, Agent Host logged the matching unknown-customization warning, no process spawned, and the clicked row remained stuck at `Starting`.
  - Patched: the UI dispatched the same workspace ID, no unknown-customization warning was logged, a new real MCP process spawned, the workspace entry transitioned `stopped -> starting -> ready`, and the clicked row reached `Running`.
  - A separate `solo` server completed stop/start successfully as a control.
- The patched live arm was repeated through the repository's normal `scripts/code.bat` launch path with the same result.

Current source combines user and `.vscode/mcp.json` inputs before Agent Host receives them, so the live harness used a host-configured plugin child plus workspace-root `.mcp.json` to deterministically reproduce the same published child/top-level identity collision described by the issue.

title: Fix per-turn chat diff reloads
body:
## Summary

Fix completed per-turn change summaries changing or disappearing when switching Agent sessions.

Completed response rows were mixing three lifecycle-dependent views of a turn: provisional tool-edit totals, the authoritative per-turn checkpoint diff, and the active Sessions Changes view's mutable last-turn changeset. Session activation caused the UI to switch between these sources, so counts could change (for example `+77/-33` to `+76/-32`) or resolve to zero and hide the summary.

This change makes the per-request checkpoint diff the single source of truth for a completed response's header, file list, visibility, and open action. Default Agent Host chats now wait for the authoritative checkpoint rather than flashing provisional raw-edit totals. Peer-chat and failed-checkpoint fallbacks remain supported.

## Root cause

#332297 added raw response edits as a temporary fallback while the server-computed turn changeset was loading. Raw edit totals count intermediate operations and can differ from the final net checkpoint diff.

#332759 then routed the latest response header through the active Sessions Changes view while leaving its file list on the per-request provider. Because Changes subscriptions are gated by the active session, switching sessions caused an immutable completed response to follow a mutable active-session changeset.

#332982 correctly made authoritative empty results clear cached summaries, which exposed the existing race as a disappearing row.

The existing tests covered each mechanism independently, but did not model the combined lifecycle: a restored response row rendering provisional response edits, activating its session, and then receiving a different or empty checkpoint changeset.

## Fix

- Remove the active Changes-view stats override.
- Derive completed-turn counts from the same per-request diffs used by the file list.
- Wait for authoritative checkpoint diffs for default chats while changesets are loading.
- Preserve response-edit fallback for peer chats and checkpoint failures.
- Add regression coverage for provisional `+77/-33` response totals resolving directly to authoritative `+76/-32` totals without rendering the provisional state.

## Result

- Opening or switching sessions no longer changes a completed turn's counts.
- A restored row stays hidden until its authoritative checkpoint arrives instead of flashing provisional totals.
- Once an authoritative diff has rendered, temporary recompute/reconnect states retain it.
- An authoritative no-op turn can still correctly clear/hide the summary.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client`
- `npm run hygiene`
- 26 focused tests across `SessionTurnChanges`, `ChatTurnPillsContentPart`, and `AgentHostResponseFileChangesProvider`
- Pre-commit hygiene hook
- `git diff --check`

title: agentHost: publish client tools before starting turns
body:
## Summary

- wait for the active-client customization scope to resolve and publish before dispatching new or resumed Agent Host turns
- prevent the first provider request from using a stale tool inventory when a client plugin finishes resolving during send
- avoid retaining cancelled unresolved claims and join concurrent resumes instead of dispatching a stale duplicate
- add ordering, cancellation, and resume-concurrency regressions

## What this waits for

The new barrier waits only for **client-side customization resolution and publication**: discovering plugin/skill/instruction/MCP configuration metadata, preparing any synced plugin bundle, and sending the resulting `session/activeClientSet` before `chat/turnStarted`.

It does **not** wait for an MCP server to connect, authenticate, complete its initialize handshake, or return `tools/list`. Those network-facing steps happen afterward inside the Copilot runtime and retain the runtime's existing timeout behavior; this PR does not add to or change that wait.

With the actual local `vscode-corpus` plugin (9 MCP servers / 83 declared tools), the fixed run published the Corpus customization 74 ms after submit. Submit-to-turn-start was 515 ms with the fix versus 472 ms on the parent (+43 ms), while submit-to-first-model-request was 55 ms faster with the fix, putting the observed difference within normal run-to-run noise. See the [real Corpus timing details](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/334385#issuecomment-5546650938).

## Summary

title: [typescript] Add setting to include closing braces in folding ranges
body:
Solves #3352 for TypeScript/JavaScript. Adds `js/ts.folding.includeClosingBraces` (false) to `typescript-language-features`, allowing users to control whether closing braces and tags are included in folding regions. Historically, and due to the workaround for #47240, the TypeScript extension excludes closing braces from folding regions. As a result, collapsed code blocks leave the closing-brace lines visible as a separate line. This change allows users who prefer code blocks to collapse to a single line, as requested in #3352, to opt into that behavior. For example, many users prefer the collapsed code to look like the right side of the provided screenshot, rather than the current behavior shown on the left:
The change only extends code folding ranges that were affected by the #47240 workaround, leaving comment, region, and import folding ranges intact. It also accounts for adjacent folding regions, avoiding changes that would corrupt folding of constructs such as `if () { ... } else { ... }`, which produce multiple adjacent regions, by checking that extending a region does not overlap another existing region. This is implemented in the `typescript-language-features` extension rather than in VS Code's core folding implementation. The current direction is not to modify folding ranges on the VS Code side or introduce a common, language-agnostic folding-preferences carrier API for folding range providers, as proposed in #298676. Consequently, extensions need to expose their own settings for such folding preferences. There are several folding extensions available in the Marketplace, but some are broken and have been unmaintained for a long time. The ones that still partially work are generally based on regular expressions rather than syntax-aware folding, and are not aware of language-specific exclusions. For example, the best configuration I found for TypeScript is the [ExplicitFolding](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=zokugun.explicit-folding) extension: https://gist.github.com/n-gist/7a7fed4f9ef90a5e7e31c1879f88efc4. The regular expression is already complex and difficult to maintain, yet it still fails in some cases. When a case it cannot handle is encountered in a file, all subsequent folding regions are broken. Since the folding provider currently has no test coverage, I did not introduce a new test area as part of this change. I am attaching a file with the test cases I used to manually verify the changes with the setting enabled and disabled. - Move eligible workspace server entries from `.vscode/mcp.json` to workspace-root `.mcp.json` so the active Agent Host harness can discover them directly.
- Show source and destination before confirmation, preserve selection and keyboard focus across refreshes, and leave unsupported or unselected servers in place.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Eligibility and editor integration

The migration service extends its existing support reporting with executable MCP candidates. Candidates must be enabled, applicable to the session, client-forwarded, fully supported, and exactly representable in the destination format. The source configuration must match the current Agent Host delivery projection without losing properties or relying on unresolved configuration variables.

MCP entries reuse the editor's existing virtualized migration lists, grouping, selection, confirmation, and notification flow. They are server entries rather than customization files, so rows show a name and source-to-destination path without file-specific actions. Existing prompt, user-data, and configured-location migration behavior is preserved.

### Session context and URI routing

The service recomputes eligibility after confirmation and checks the active session and ordered working-directory roots before and between writes. The support scope remains live during execution. Guards compare coverage and the pending candidates' delivery eligibility and projected configuration, rather than support-snapshot object identity, so equivalent snapshot refreshes do not abort migration merely because a new object was published.

`IAgentHostCustomizationService.getWorkingDirectoryUris` derives client-resolvable roots in the shared abstract service. Existing root getters retain host-side URI strings for workspace classification and protocol enablement decisions. The Agents Window uses the provider's stable resource mapper instead of depending on a feedback channel or falling back to identity mapping, preventing remote roots from being mistaken for matching local paths.

Workbench root resolution uses provisional roots until session state is available and falls back to the subscription's verified state on errors. MCP computation honors caller cancellation while waiting for initial support resolution, checks cancellation around planning, and disposes the acquired support scope.

### Write safety and failure handling

Each source/destination pair is handled as a guarded two-file update:

1. Re-read the source and destination, reject changed source entries and conflicting destination entries.
2. Write missing destination entries first, or accept equivalent entries already present.
3. Recheck execution context before removing the selected source entries.
4. Re-read both files to verify the result; restore original content only when doing so is safe.

Existing wrapped (`mcpServers`) and flat JSONC `.mcp.json` files are accepted. Edits preserve surrounding comments and formatting. Existing-file writes compare exact expected content and use file-service etag/mtime guards; new-file creation does not overwrite an existing destination.

These are best-effort optimistic-concurrency checks, not an atomic cross-file transaction. If rollback cannot be performed safely, the operation reports a structured failure and asks the user to review the affected files. A newly created destination is retained rather than deleted during rollback. Planning exclusions and execution phases are trace-logged for diagnosis.

</details>

## Summary

This updates every page in the AI Customizations management editor to use independent virtualized `WorkbenchList` controls while preserving each page's existing structure and actions.

## Reviewer walkthrough

### 1. Shared virtualized section behavior

- Adds reusable section-list layout helpers in `customizationCardList.ts`.
- Distributes the available viewport height across all expanded sections instead of relying on an outer scrolling region.
- Reserves at least one complete row for each populated section, then water-fills the remaining height based on content.
- Redistributes freed space immediately when a section is collapsed or expanded.
- Uses stable loading placeholders so asynchronous item discovery does not initially collapse sections to tiny slivers.
- Preserves each list's scroll position during layout, refreshes, filtering-related rerenders, and collapse/expand cycles.

### 2. Page coverage

- **Agents, Skills, Instructions, Hooks, and Prompts:** each storage/source group is its own virtualized list.

- **MCP Servers:** Featured, Installed, and Available sections remain separate and virtualized; existing server status badges are preserved.
- **Tools:** each tool provider section uses its own virtualized list with dynamic row heights.
- **Migration pages:** User and Workspace migration groups use virtualized lists while retaining selection, Select All, open, overflow, and migration actions.

### 3. Collapsible sections and height coordination

- Makes all section headers, including Featured sections, collapsible and expanded by default.
- Keeps header labels, counts, descriptions, badges, create/install actions, and overflow actions intact.
- Fixes disclosure state so the region actually hides, including layouts whose explicit display rules previously overrode the native `hidden` attribute.
- Uses a consistent spacing-ramp gap between sections in both expanded and collapsed states.
- Avoids conflicting inner and outer scrollbars by constraining scrolling to the section lists.

### 4. Row presentation and actions

- Restores the recessed row tint while preserving standard hover, focus, and selection colors.
- Keeps installed Plugin and MCP row actions horizontally aligned, with the enablement toggle before the ellipsis menu.
- Removes the resting button border around row ellipsis actions.

- Removes the legacy extra gap between Featured and Installed Plugins.

### 6. Lifecycle, keyboard, and accessibility details

- Clears stale list registrations before asynchronous rerenders so hidden/disposed lists do not consume height.
- Stores direct layout-container references instead of querying recreated DOM.
- Retains virtualized-list accessibility providers, item counts, positions, keyboard navigation, and focus restoration.

title: Add `editor.textDirection` to lay out editor contents right-to-left
body:
Part of #4994 and #11770. See also #270580, which specifies this design.

VS Code can be localized into right-to-left languages, but the editor has no way to lay out its
**contents** right-to-left. The direction of a line is inferred per line, so a file written in
Arabic, Hebrew, Persian or Urdu renders as a stack of independently-resolved paragraphs: the caret
starts on the wrong side, a line beginning with an identifier or a symbol flips to left-to-right,
and line numbers and glyph margin stay on the left of text that reads from the right.

### The option

`editor.textDirection: 'auto' | 'ltr' | 'rtl' | 'uiLanguage'`

| value | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `auto` (default) | **exactly today's behaviour**: lines are laid out left-to-right |
| `ltr` | the same as `auto` today; the explicit counterpart of `rtl`, and the value to reach for to opt one language out of a broader `rtl` |
| `rtl` | lines are laid out right-to-left and the editor mirrors its layout (table below) |
| `uiLanguage` | `rtl` when the user interface is itself displayed in a right-to-left language |

A line whose direction a decoration declares keeps that direction under **every** value, exactly as
it does today. That is also why `auto` and `ltr` coincide: nothing here infers direction from
content, so both resolve to a left-to-right layout.

The setting is language-overridable, which is usually the scope it wants — direction is a property
of what a file contains, not of the window.

What `rtl` moves, and what it does not:

| element | `ltr` | `rtl` | |
|---|---|---|---|
| line numbers, glyph margin, folding | left edge | right edge, **and mirrored inside the strip**: reading outwards from the text come decorations, then line numbers, then the glyph margin | mirrored |
| minimap | side set by `minimap.side` | left edge, with its canvases flipped so the shape it paints matches the text. `minimap.side` is not honoured, and its description now says so | mirrored |
| text of each line | left-to-right | right-to-left, via a per-line `dir` attribute set by `ViewLine` | mirrored |
| vertical scrollbar | right of the content | right of the content | **unchanged** |
| overview ruler | with the scrollbar | with the scrollbar | **unchanged** |

The scrollbar staying put is deliberate: right-to-left lines already reserve `verticalScrollbarWidth`
with `padding-right` in `ViewLine#renderLine`, which predates this PR, so moving the bar would
reserve one side and paint on the other. The overview ruler annotates the scrollbar, so it stays
with it.

### Changing the direction of one file

`View: Change Editor Text Direction`, also in the View menu next to Word Wrap. It cycles the active
editor between the direction its settings give it, right-to-left, and left-to-right.

It is built like `toggleWordWrap`, and for the same reason: direction is not really a property of a
language. A repository holds an English README and an Arabic guide, both Markdown, and a
per-language setting cannot tell them apart. So the command writes **transient per-model state**
rather than settings — it never edits a `.vscode/settings.json` that is checked into git — and a new
editor option `textDirectionOverride: 'inherit' | 'auto' | 'ltr' | 'rtl'` carries that state into
`EffectiveTextDirection`. The setting remains the place to express a lasting preference.

### Why `uiLanguage` is not the default

Most people who localize the interface into Arabic, Hebrew or Persian still write Latin identifiers
all day; flipping their editor on an update, with no setting they ever touched, is not a change to
make silently. It is there for the people who do want it, as a value they choose.

### How it is built

- **The internal coordinate system is unchanged.** The editor still measures from a physical left
  origin. The mirrored layout is applied by the view parts and by CSS guarded on a
  `text-direction-rtl` class that `EditorClassName` contributes.
- **One physical origin.** In a mirrored layout the minimap occupies the leading strip, the content
  box starts where it ends, and the margin is flush with the right edge. Hit testing, content
  widgets, block decorations and the drag-select boundaries all derive that origin the same way.
- **Decorations still win, per line.** `ViewModel._getTextDirection` returns a decoration-declared
  direction when there is one — resolved exactly as before, ties included — and falls back to the
  option only for lines that declare none. Indent guides, sticky lines and the GPU renderer's
  fallback check the line's direction, not the layout's.
- **`EffectiveTextDirection`** is a computed option, so the setting is resolved once rather than at
  each read site.
- Exposed on `IEditorOptions`, so the Monaco standalone editor gets the setting too.

### Size, and what this does not change

21 files in the editor plus one new workbench contribution. 85 of the added lines are generated
(`standaloneEnums.ts` renumbering and `monaco.d.ts`); the rest is hand-written, most of it in the
view parts.

Two generated lines look unrelated and are not. Registering a new option shifts the order in which
TypeScript prints an unrelated union in `monaco.d.ts`, and `compile-src` fails the build when the
checked-in file does not match the generator. I verified this with the generator's own `execute()`:
on `main` untouched it reports `isTheSame: true`, with this branch applied and those lines reverted
it reports `false`, and with them as committed it reports `true` again.

**No change to default rendering.** With the setting at `auto` the resolved direction is always
`ltr`, whatever the display language. `editorLayoutProvider.test.ts` asserts that the mirrored
layout differs from the left-to-right one *only* in the order of the margin strip's children.

### Known limits

These are real, and I would rather name them than have them found:

- **Widgets that sit over the editor are not mirrored**: peek, inline chat, the inside of the find
  widget. They read as left-to-right panels above a mirrored editor rather than as broken layout.
- **Word-wise cursor movement is not direction-aware.** `wordOperations` has no notion of direction
  today, so `Ctrl+Left` moves against `Left` on a right-to-left line. This is pre-existing — it
  already applies to decoration-declared right-to-left lines — but this PR makes it reachable for
  whole files. It needs its own change, with the delete-word and select-word commands alongside.
- **IME and screen-reader anchoring** compute their position from `contentLeft`, which is the width
  of the margin strip rather than the content origin once the layout is mirrored. Five call sites
  across the edit contexts; also better as its own change.
- **Performance**: a right-to-left line takes neither the GPU renderer nor `ViewLine`'s fast path,
  as a line containing right-to-left characters already does not.

### Relationship to #318214

An earlier version of this description said the two PRs touch disjoint files. That was wrong:
#318214 also registers `editor.textDirection` and edits `editorOptions.ts`, `viewModelImpl.ts` and
`monaco.d.ts`, so they overlap on the option contract and need to be sequenced.

The contracts differ. #318214 registers `'ltr' | 'rtl' | 'auto'` defaulting to `'ltr'`, with `auto`
meaning first-strong-character detection per line. This PR registers
`'auto' | 'ltr' | 'rtl' | 'uiLanguage'` defaulting to `'auto'`, where `auto` is today's behaviour
unchanged. Beyond the option, this PR has what #318214 does not: the mirrored layout, view parts,
hit testing and CSS. I can rebase on #318214 and drop this registration, or fold the two —
whichever you prefer.

### Test

Set `"editor.textDirection": "rtl"` and open a file with Arabic or Hebrew text. Verify: line numbers
on the right with the glyph margin outside them, minimap on the left showing the same shape as the
text, caret on the right of an empty line, ruler columns measured from the right, a click on a line
number selecting the line rather than toggling a breakpoint, and the vertical scrollbar still on the
right of the content. Then run `View: Change Editor Text Direction` twice and confirm that nothing
is left behind and that no settings file changed.

title: Agent Host: stop the reconnecting banner nagging on a flapping transport
body:
A coworker reported a reconnecting banner appearing constantly on a session that otherwise worked fine. Their tunnel relay was dropping and restoring the transport on a ~6s cycle — each outage healed in ~2s with session state preserved, so the chat kept working the whole time.

Two separate causes, both from #334111.

## Stale outage start time

The outage start lives in a `derivedObservableWithCache`. While the host is connected nothing reads the reconnecting state, so that derived lost its observers — and a derived that is not observed keeps its last value without ever recomputing it. The next outage read `last?.session === session`, matched, and reused the *previous* outage's timestamp. The delay had therefore already elapsed, so the banner appeared immediately.

That is why it looked constant rather than merely frequent: only the first outage was ever debounced.

Fixed with `recomputeInitiallyAndOnChange`, which keeps the derived observed for the lifetime of the view so it recomputes on reconnect. The derived and its session keying are otherwise unchanged.

## Threshold shorter than a routine reconnect

`RECONNECTING_BANNER_DELAY` was 1s, but a self-healed reconnect here took ~2.05s. The delay exists to suppress blips the user would not otherwise notice — a reconnect that preserves session state is exactly that — so 1s was mistuned. Raised to 5s, comfortably past an observed reconnect.

Both changes are needed: with only the longer delay, a 2s outage still shows the banner on every cycle after the first, because the stale timestamp makes the delay a no-op.

## Test

`stays quiet while a flapping transport keeps healing itself` replays the reported cadence (2.1s outage, 3.7s healthy, five cycles) and asserts the banner never appears. It fails with either fix reverted — the stale-cache bug reproduces as the banner appearing from the second cycle onward.

The underlying relay instability (`[TunnelAgentHost] onDidRelayClose`) is pre-existing and out of scope here; this only stops the UI nagging about a connection that is working.

title: Fix RemotePty.resize dropping the last resize of an A-B-A sequence
body: Refs #325743, #239310 ### Problem https://disk.yandex.ru/i/Z-KpZ2owm_4hEg Showing a hidden **maximized** panel leaves a **remote** terminal (Remote-SSH / Dev Containers) with a pty at the *restored* height while xterm.js is at the maximized height, so TUIs such as tmux paint only the top part of the panel. The next hide/show repairs it, and it strictly alternates. Local terminals are not affected. ### Root cause `setPanelHidden(false)` lays the terminal out at the restored size and immediately re-maximizes it within the same task, so `RemotePty.resize` is called with F, R, F from consecutive microtasks (`setVisible(true) -> _resize()` with the stale size, `composite.layout(contentAreaSize)`, then `toggleMaximizedPanel()`). `RemotePty.resize` compared the requested size against `_lastDimensions` synchronously but only assigned `_lastDimensions` inside `_startBarrier.wait().then(...)`, one microtask later. So the first F was dropped as identical, R passed, and the final F was compared against the not-yet-updated `_lastDimensions` and dropped as well. Only R reached the pty host. `LocalPty.resize` assigns `_lastDimensions` synchronously before calling the proxy, which is why the symptom is remote-only. ### Fix Assign `_lastDimensions` synchronously in `RemotePty.resize`, mirroring `LocalPty`, and add a regression test for the A-B-A case (and for deduping identical consecutive sizes, which was also broken within one turn). ### Notes The test was not run locally (no build environment on the machine where this was authored); it targets the same shape as `agentHostPty.test.ts`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Add opt-in auto-archive/delete inactive sessions with merged pull requests
body:
## Summary

This PR adds two application-scoped Preview settings for inactive agent sessions that have at least one merged pull request and no open related pull requests:

- `chat.agentSessions.autoArchiveMergedSessionsAfterDays`
  - disabled by default (`0`)
  - accepts any positive whole number of inactive days; 15 is the recommended value
  - archives eligible sessions through the normal archive lifecycle, including safe worktree cleanup and provider notification
- `chat.agentSessions.autoDeleteArchivedMergedSessionsAfterDays`
  - disabled by default (`0`)
  - accepts any positive whole number for the separate post-archive deletion grace period; 15 is the recommended value
  - permanently deletes only sessions that carry durable automatic-archive provenance

Worktree cleanup is part of archiving rather than a separate setting. If a retained worktree is still present when permanent deletion becomes eligible, deletion applies the same safe cleanup first.

## Lifecycle behavior

- lifecycle candidates are prefiltered from durable session metadata before restoring sessions
- active and external sessions are excluded
- every related pull request is refreshed before restoration and again immediately before lifecycle side effects, so reopening a closed PR blocks the action
- no related pull request may be open, and at least one must be merged; closed-unmerged PRs do not block cleanup once another related PR has merged
- archive/delete settings, session state, retention periods, and pull request identity are revalidated after session restoration
- automatic deletion applies only to sessions carrying durable automatic-archive provenance
- manually archived sessions are never made deletion-eligible by this lifecycle
- unarchiving clears automatic-archive provenance
- automatic archive uses the normal archive action and side-effect path
- deletion cleans a retained worktree inside the disposal critical section, where concurrent unarchive is rejected
- deletion uses the persisted primary repository root when removing checkpoint/review refs, including after worktree cleanup and Agent Host restart
- startup/hourly evaluation remains active when either lifecycle setting is enabled

## Worktree cleanup safety

Archiving or deleting an eligible session removes its worktree only when Git reports all of the following:

- the worktree has a branch
- the branch tracks an upstream
- outgoing and uncommitted change counts are both known
- there are zero outgoing commits
- there are zero uncommitted changes

Incoming commits do not block cleanup. Missing or unknown Git state fails closed. Cleanup uses ordinary, non-force `git worktree remove`, so Git performs a final dirty-worktree check as well. The lifecycle does not commit local changes or force-remove the worktree.

Removing a worktree is reversible for an archived session: the checkout can be recreated when the session is unarchived.

## User experience

Both settings default to disabled, so sessions remain visible, are not automatically archived, and are not permanently deleted.

The existing one-time **Turn On Session Cleanup** notification appears for an eligible merged-PR session after 15 days of inactivity while both settings are disabled. Its actions are:

- **Turn On Session Cleanup**: sets archive and delete thresholds to 15 days
- **Open Settings**: opens the `chat.agentSessions.auto*` settings

## Validation

- client transpilation
- focused Agent Host lifecycle tests
- AgentService unit tests
- targeted ESLint for changed TypeScript files
- `git diff --check`

title: agent host: stop chat queues from wedging on a non-settling SDK RPC
body:
agent host: stop chat queues from wedging on a non-settling SDK RPC

All chat operations for one chat serialize on a single per-chat sequencer. A control-plane RPC in that
queue had no timeout, so an RPC that never settled kept the queue head forever. Every later send,
model change, and abort stayed queued and never ran. The client showed a turn that stayed active with
no response and no error. Abort shared the same queue, so Cancel could not recover the chat.

- Bounds the short SDK control-plane RPCs at 30 seconds through a new `_awaitControlPlaneRpc` helper.
  This covers `session.setModel`, `rpc.agent.select`, `rpc.agent.deselect`, and `rpc.history.truncate`.
  A timeout now rejects the operation and lets the queue continue. Turn delivery through `session.send`
  stays unbounded, because a turn can correctly run for a long time.
- Removes abort from the per-chat queue. Abort must interrupt a blocked queue, so it cannot wait behind
  the task it must cancel.
- Adds an operation name to each `_queueChat` call and logs a warning if a queue task runs for more than
  60 seconds. The warning names the operation that holds the queue.
- Adds regression tests for the timeout, for a queued send that continues after a timeout, and for an
  abort that completes while a queue task is blocked.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/334159

title: agentHost: scale E2E protocol timeouts for CI contention
body:
Fixes the Agent Host E2E failures in [build 470786](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=470786&view=logs&j=193e9987-1fae-53fa-a82e-3ae14c27c30d&t=947af107-991d-500d-0eee-76fd05e265dc).

## What failed

The Linux Electron integration step lost four E2E tests across three parallel suites. None was a wrong result; every one was a wait expiring:

- **Codex**, after-each hook for `archiving a never-restored session survives a host restart`: cleanup called `subscribe` on a session never re-subscribed after two host restarts, so the host had to restore it from disk first, and the 5s default expired.
- **Claude**, `session changeset aggregates provider edits from default and peer chats`: `createChat` hit the 5s default. Every other suite already passes 30s for that call.
- **Claude**, `a GitHub remote with changes advertises pull request creation`: create-pr was not advertised within the ~10s poll.
- **Conformance**, `a client can clear review state from a changed file`: the review-changed notification did not arrive within 5s.

The run was starved. All four suites start at the same second on one agent, and this run took roughly twice as long as neighbouring runs (Copilot suite 312s vs. 165–214s).

## Cause

Not a single commit. The exact `Failed to release ... Timeout waiting for response to subscribe` signature already appeared on main on 2026-08-27 (Copilot) and 2026-09-02 (Claude, Windows), predating the recent Copilot, Codex and Claude SDK bumps. What changed is load: E2E coverage grew substantially on 2026-09-02, running four-wide against a default protocol timeout that scaled for Windows and coverage mode but never for CI.

## Fix

Waits are made environment-aware; no assertion changes.

- `serverIntegrationTestHelpers.ts`: default protocol operation timeout is 20s on CI. Local stays 5s (8s on Windows) so a wedged host still fails fast. Nothing relies on the default firing for a negative assertion. `fetchSessionWithChat` gains an optional timeout.
- `agentHostE2ETestHarness.ts`: `release()` uses the extended cleanup bound for its subscribe calls, matching the dispose calls, so a slow cleanup no longer fails a passing test and forces a server restart.
- `changesetSuite.ts`: operation polling allows 300 retries on CI, and the peer-chat `createChat` passes 30s like its siblings.

## Verification

ESLint and TypeScript are clean on the changed files. The E2E suites were not run locally (no product build in the worktree); CI on this PR is the real check.

## Separate observation

Two Windows-only failures of the Claude `archiving a never-restored session survives a host restart` test on 2026-09-02/03 were real assertions (`listSessions` missing the session after restart), landing within a few builds of the Claude Agent SDK 0.3.258 bump. title: Bind MCP protected-resource metadata to the server that advertised it
body:
A pending MCP authentication request is matched to an arriving token by its `resource` value, so `resource` is what decides where that token goes. `CopilotAgentSession._protectedResourceFromMcpAuthRequest` took that value from the metadata the MCP server supplied, checked only that the JSON had the right shape, and used it as given. A server could therefore advertise a resource belonging to somewhere else and be handed the token approved for that resource.

`fetchPrm` in `base/common/oauth.ts` already refuses metadata whose `resource` does not identify the URL it was fetched for, citing RFC 9728. This path had no equivalent check, so the two disagree about whether an advertised resource has to be bound to anything. This adds the missing one.

The rule is origin plus URL prefix, not equality. Equality would be wrong here, and the existing tests show why: a server at `https://mcp.slack.com/mcp` legitimately advertises `https://mcp.slack.com` as its resource. The prefix is compared by path segment, so `https://example.com/mcp` does not cover `https://example.com/mcpx`.

Metadata that fails the check is dropped rather than the request being rejected outright, and the request falls back to the identity derived from the server's own URL, so a server can still authenticate as itself.

## Testing

`src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/mcpProtectedResourceBinding.test.ts` adds 24 cases for the binding itself: the prefix and equality shapes that should pass, host case and default port normalisation, and on the other side a different host, a host that merely shares a prefix, differing scheme or port, a path prefix that is not a segment boundary, a server above the advertised resource rather than under it, values that are not URLs, and opaque origins.

`copilotAgentSession.test.ts` adds one end-to-end test through the existing session harness: a server advertising another server's resource has the claim dropped, is not settled by a token approved for that other resource, and can still authenticate as itself. That test fails without the change.

The existing 413-test session suite still passes, including the cases that rely on a server advertising a resource that is a prefix of its URL, which is what ruled out the equality reading.

`tsc -p src` and `eslint` are clean.

## Note on reporting

This was reported through MSRC (case 128144) and closed as not meeting the definition of a vulnerability, on the basis that discovery-time validation binds the advertised resource to the server's own origin. That validation does hold in `fetchPrm`; the point of this change is that this particular path does not go through it. I am sending the change here rather than opening a public issue describing it, since SECURITY.md asks that issues not be used for this. Happy to open one if you would prefer the PR to reference it.

title: Keep MACHINE target storage keys out of applied profile content
body:
`GlobalStateResource.getGlobalState` only writes out `StorageTarget.USER` values, so a key held at `StorageTarget.MACHINE` is never something a profile produced. Applying profile content did not hold to the same rule. `GlobalStateResourceInitializer.initialize` took every key it was given, and `writeGlobalState` excluded application scope and workspace scope machine keys but not profile scope ones. Both wrote what they took at `StorageTarget.USER`.

`chat.transferedWorkspaces` is a profile scope, MACHINE target key. It is the machine's own record that a chat session was moved to a folder, and `ChatTransferService.checkAndSetTransferredWorkspaceTrust` grants that folder workspace trust on open. The read did not look at the target, so a value carried in profile content satisfied it.

Two changes, either of which closes it, both worth having:

Applying profile content now uses one shared rule for the keys it will not take, and that rule includes profile scope MACHINE keys. The initializer uses the same rule instead of taking everything. Rejecting one key no longer costs the rest of the content, which the initializer would previously not have been able to express at all.

`ChatTransferService` requires the list to be at MACHINE target before honouring it. This is the half that holds when the key is not already present on the machine, which a rule based on the keys currently known cannot see.

Not addressed here: trust is still granted from an emptiness check made before the folder is opened, so a folder that gains content in between is still trusted. That is a change to how the transfer flow decides trust rather than to which values it believes, so it seemed better kept separate.

## Testing

`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatTransferService.test.ts` adds 5 tests: a workspace the machine recorded is trusted on open; a list arriving at USER target does not grant trust; a USER target write over an existing machine record does not either; an unrelated workspace and no record at all do not.

`src/vs/workbench/services/userDataProfile/test/browser/globalStateResource.test.ts` adds 5 more: a key held at MACHINE target in profile scope is not taken and its value is left alone, the same for application scope, ordinary profile keys are still taken, and content carrying both keeps the ordinary one.

Two of them fail without the change while the rest keep passing.

title: Withhold the GnuPG sandbox grant from Git commands that can run a supplied program
body:
The agent terminal sandbox grants a Git command `allowAllUnixSockets` together with read and write access to `~/.gnupg`, so that a signing operation can reach gpg-agent and the keyring. The rule matched on the `git` keyword alone.

Git reaches gpg through a child process, and the grant is applied to the whole sandboxed process tree, so whatever Git spawns inherits it. Several ordinary parts of a Git command line choose that child: an alias whose value begins with `!` is a shell command, `core.pager`, `core.editor`, `credential.helper` and `core.hooksPath` all name programs, `--exec` and `--upload-pack` take one directly, and `git bisect run` exists to run one. A command line of the shape `git -c alias.<name>='!...' <name>` reads as an ordinary Git command to the rule and as an arbitrary shell command to Git, which then holds the keyring and every Unix socket on the machine.

The grant is now refused for those invocations. None of them is a signing operation, so nothing a signing flow needs is lost, and a command that does need signing and is refused fails visibly rather than silently running with the keyring exposed.

Points worth a reviewer's attention:

- Configuration overrides are checked against an allow list of keys that cannot name a program, rather than a deny list. Git keeps adding keys that can name one, and a deny list would sit one release behind.
- `-c` is only read as a configuration override before the subcommand. After it, `-c` belongs to the subcommand — `git commit -c <commit>` reuses a commit message — and reading that as a configuration key would refuse the grant to an ordinary signing command. `--exec`, `--upload-pack` and `--receive-pack` are the other way round: they belong to the subcommand, so the whole argument list is scanned for them.
- The subcommand is resolved with the existing `getCommandSubcommand` helper, so a subcommand's own argument cannot be mistaken for one; `git commit -m submodule` keeps the grant.
- The check runs over the whole invocation next to the existing Docker check, since the grant covers the process tree and one such command anywhere in a chain is enough to pass the keyring on.

The environment can redirect what Git runs just as effectively as the arguments can, through `GIT_CONFIG_*`, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `PATH` and others, so `TreeSitterCommandParser` now reports the assignments that prefix a command instead of discarding them, and `ITerminalSandboxCommand` carries them. The field is left off entirely when there are none, so the common shape is unchanged.

One consequence worth calling out explicitly, since it is a behaviour change rather than a pure tightening: an invocation carrying one of those assignments no longer receives the grant, and that includes `GIT_EDITOR=true git commit -S`. The command still runs sandboxed; it just does not get the keyring. I took the fail-closed reading here, but that is a judgement call and I am happy to narrow the list if you would rather keep those working.

## Testing

`src/vs/platform/sandbox/test/common/terminalSandboxRuntimeConfigurationPerOperation.test.ts` adds 49 tests.
